newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX stung by Wall Street decline.
newsitem.headline: German DAX stung by Wall Street decline.

text.p: German shares opened lower on Friday as overnight weakness on Wall Street and a touch of pre-weekend catharsis hit sentiment on the stock exchange.
The DAX index was down 33.95 points, or 0.75 percent, at 4,381.00 points after an hour of bourse trade, while the September DAX future stood at 4,393 points, down 52 points.
"We've seen some profit-taking initially," said one trader.
"Volumes are quieter than they have been, and we don't see too much dramatic action. The banks are the big movers."
Bank shares were outperforming amid a fresh wave of takeover speculation which most dealers dismissed as idle chatter but which nonetheless pushed financials ahead.
Commerzbank, always a favourite subject of takeover talk, was leading volumes and trading ahead against the trend at 65.40 marks, up 1.95 marks or three percent.
Various buyers were being mooted for Commerzbank, including the large Swiss banks, rival Deutsche Bank and HSBC.
Dresdner Bank was also up 1.10 marks at 81.80 marks and Bayerische Vereinsbank AG was up 90 pfennigs at 97.60 marks.
Losses were otherwise spread across all sectors.
Dealers were mainly unfazed by the weakness of prices, saying this was typical of the end to a slow week.
"It's healthy to have a bit of a sell-off, but I think we may even have a bit of a rally this afternoon," said one dealer.
